newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia blast injures five, rebels killed.
newsitem.headline: Colombia blast injures five, rebels killed.

text.p: Two bombs exploded in northeastern Colombia early on Wednesday, injuring five people, in the latest dynamite attacks by leftist guerrillas, police said.
The blasts shook downtown Bucaramanga on the day that President Ernesto Samper and National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano were scheduled to visit the city in Santander province.
"Terrorism has arrived in our city. This marks the escalation of a wave of bombings in the east of the country," Bucaramanga mayor Carlos Ibanez said.
In a separate incident in the northern coal-mining province of Cesar, soldiers freed three kidnapped Colombian engineers and killed three leftist rebels, military sources said.
In Bucaramanga, a police spokesman said two men were captured shortly after the explosions, which damaged the office of a cattle ranchers' association and the chamber of commerce.
He said the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest rebel group, was thought to be behind the attacks.
The attacks took place 24 hours after two car bombs exploded in Cucuta, in neighbouring Norte de Santander province, killing an 18-month-old girl.

In Cesar province, troops freed the three engineers on Tuesday afternoon after a gunfight with Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels in a rural area near the town of Codazzi, an army spokesman said. Two guerrillas died in the clash.
A National Liberation Army (ELN) rebel was killed in fighting near the town of Aguachica in the same province.
